HOW IS THIS GAME IN 2021? A great game for the Warhammer fan! If you are new to Warhammer, then some things and sayings likely won't have any effect on you. But this in no way affects the progression and gameplay or understanding. Kill all the green guys (Orks). The combat is decent, fast-paced and the glory/rage kills plenty. I still find new death animations to this day! A small range of guns and handheld weapons help saw, cut, and explode green body parts across the vast manufacturing ........ World I think. I am not sure if it is a planet or a giant factory.  Or maybe the factory is the planet! THAT'S NO MOON! 
Anyhow Gameplay mechanics are I don't want to say you're basic hack and slash. But kinda and feels a little repetitive at times. I believe this is mainly due to the landscape and scenery never changing. It's a factory, it's grey and that's about it. Some small lore details can be found. 
I cranked the setting up to 2k and high and was getting 200fps lol - That being said, this game is easy to run at high frames and resolutions. Mostly due to its age. The 3d models still look clean and not from a 10-year-old game. Mostly the age of the game is shown in the textures of the landscape. Not enough to take you out of the game. But it's also not amazing. 
BIGGEST ISSUE! - The bankruptcy of THQ and no 2nd or 3rd installment. The online DLC is fun but not many people play. You have to check the community and forums to find online games. Jumping into an online game randomly did not yield any results. No-fault of the game, just age. 

I recommend this game to any Warhammer fan or not. 100% a buy if its on sale

P.S - How does this compare to the PS#3 version? - BETTER FRAMES, BETTER IMAGE QUALITY, And Faster Load times compared to PS3 - PS3 Main advantage is the game can be found used sometimes for under $10 and is still great fun with mild hiccups and slowdowns. Not worth the extra cost if you own the Steam version
I love this game. Why was there no continuation? At least do a remaster, please!

Introduction:

This is another great game from another great year in gaming (2011). This is one of a few Warhammer 40k games that I personally think are absolutely necessary to play if you want to get into Warhammer 40k. The story is kind of bland and forgettable, but the hack and slash and third person shooter gameplay is absolutely amazing.

Story and Gameplay (Spoilers):

The story as mentioned above is alright, but nothing too memorable. The game follows a squad of Ultramarines led by Captain Titus, the soft spoken but stern player character, Sergeant Sidonus, an absolute bro and voice of reason in the party, and Leandros, a turbo nerd Space Marine who bases his entire character around fanatically following the Codex Astartes. The game opens up with an Ork invasion on the forge world of Graia, led by Ork Warboss Grimskull. Grimskull is one of my favorite characters in the game because of how over the top and entertaining he is, especially by Ork standards. The Orks are invading Graia to capture and loot an imperial war titan by the name of Invictus. Immediately at the beginning of the game, we see what the game has to offer in terms of gameplay. The hack and slash elements are near perfect. I would say that the gameplay is a combination of both Gears of War and Devil May Cry. There is a little bit of jank that keeps it from being perfect, and it's a bit too linear, but overall, the gameplay is very well executed. 

At one point in the game, we meet inquisitor Drogan, a 'twist' villain in the game. I know the intention of Drogan's character was to set up a character that is supposed to shock you with his betrayal, but honestly, I saw his treachery coming from a mile away. His overall mannerisms and personality came off as really suspicious from the start and I did not trust his character at all. Once Drogan inevitably betrays you, we are introduced to the main antagonist of the game, Chaos Lord Nemeroth. Nemeroth is an incredibly boring villain that puts me to sleep with his constant monologuing, and is easily my least favorite part of the game. I did enjoy fighting the forces of Chaos as well as the Orks, but Chaos has a few annoying enemies to deal with, such as Bloat Drones and the Tainted Psykers. After defeating Grimskull in an alright boss fight, we confront Nemeroth, and his boss fight sucks as much as he does. The entire thing is an incredibly easy boss fight that was over with in 5 minutes. After we beat Nemeroth, the game ends with [spoiler] Titus being detained by the inquisition to be investigated for heresy. I honestly thought this was a terrible ending and an insult to Titus's character. [/spoiler]

Final Thoughts (Spoiler Free): 

This game has fantastic gameplay and an okay story. The game focuses more on what it is good at, which is the combat, and I respect that about it. It's also a bit short and pretty easy overall, even on hard mode, but the satisfying gameplay kept me coming back to it.

Final Rating: 8/10

2021 - amidst neverending lockdowns, I've taken the time to revisit a lot of games in my library, this was one of them. 10 years post release, you can still get a game of Exterminatus (horde mode) in under 5 minutes! To this day, no other game has tried or succeeded to capture the feeling of being a vessel of joyous destruction against the emperor's foes quite the same. Customisation in MP is great and the campaign is a nice fun, short, brutal experience. Kinda like a third-person doom, set in everyone's favourite grimdark universe. There's even a great sense of RP to playing Exterminatus mode - customise your warrior and set about combatting endless green hordes and occasional traitor scum until you are vanquished.. or redeployed.
